data.final_week_advice: Focus on timed practice and mixed review to solidify retention of all units before the exam.
data.summary: This six-week plan systematically covers all nine units of AP Chemistry, starting with foundational atomic structure and progressing through reactions, kinetics, and thermodynamics. Live classes are integrated into weeks 1 and 3 to reinforce key concepts in intermolecular forces and chemical reactions. The final two weeks are dedicated to mixed review and timed practice to ensure exam readiness.

weeks.focus: Master atomic structure and introductory intermolecular forces.
tasks: Complete 20 multiple-choice questions on moles and molar mass, checking each answer against the official key.
Draw Lewis diagrams for 10 different molecules, including those with resonance structures.
Do 10 free-response questions on photoelectron spectroscopy, then mark them against the scoring guide.
Attend live class #9500 on intermolecular forces and take detailed notes on hydrogen bonding.
Solve 5 problems calculating the composition of mixtures using mass percent and empirical formulas.

weeks.focus: Deepen understanding of compound structure and gas laws.
tasks: Create a comparison chart for ionic, covalent, and metallic bonds, including examples and properties.
Do 15 multiple-choice questions on VSEPR theory and hybridization, focusing on molecular geometry.
Solve 8 ideal gas law problems involving pressure, volume, and temperature changes.
Write net ionic equations for 10 different precipitation reactions, balancing each one carefully.
Analyze 3 kinetic molecular theory diagrams to explain particle behavior in different states of matter.
Attend live class #9501 on chemical reactions and take notes on net ionic equations.
Do 10 free-response questions on stoichiometry, including limiting reactant calculations.
Write balanced molecular and net ionic equations for 12 different chemical reactions.
Solve 5 problems involving physical and chemical changes, identifying the type of change in each case.
Complete a practice set of 15 multiple-choice questions on reaction representations and stoichiometry.
Do 10 free-response questions on reaction rates and rate laws, marking them against the scoring guide.
Solve 8 problems calculating heat transfer and thermal equilibrium using calorimetry data.
Analyze 5 energy diagrams to identify endothermic and exothermic processes.
Write rate laws for 6 different elementary reactions, determining the order of each reactant.
Complete 12 multiple-choice questions on concentration changes over time and reaction mechanisms.
Do 10 free-response questions on equilibrium constants and reaction quotients, marking them against the scoring guide.
Solve 8 problems calculating pH and pOH of strong and weak acids and bases.
Write equilibrium expressions for 10 different reversible reactions, identifying the direction of shift.
Analyze 5 buffer systems to explain how they resist changes in pH.
Complete 15 multiple-choice questions on acid-base reactions and buffer capacity.

weeks.focus: Mixed review and timed practice for exam readiness.
tasks: Complete a full timed practice exam (3 hours) covering all units, then review incorrect answers.
Do 20 mixed free-response questions from all units, marking them against the scoring guide.
Review notes and flashcards for thermodynamics and electrochemistry, focusing on entropy and Gibbs free energy.
Solve 10 mixed multiple-choice questions on electrochemical cells, including galvanic and electrolytic cells.
Conduct a final review of weak areas identified in the practice exam, spending 2 hours on targeted practice.
